children: Kraken has said trades executed during a prolonged slump in its Canadian-dollar markets will stand, after bitcoin changed hands on the exchange at C$24,250 on Saturday.

The low was printed on Kraken's BTC/CAD pair while bitcoin was trading above $55,000 against the US dollar on the same platform. CryptoSlate estimated the C$24,250 print was about 71% below the prevailing Canadian-dollar value.
What Kraken said
In a post on X at 11:12 UK time on 21 November 2026, Kraken Support said CAD pairs had seen "heavy selling pressure that pushed prices well below other markets" from around 20:00 UTC on 20 November.
"Our platform processed every order correctly, and our security teams found no sign of a breach or compromised accounts. Executed trades stand," the company said.
Kraken did not say what drove the selling, or whether it would take any further steps for clients who sold at the depressed prices.
How the dislocation unfolded
Kraken's public candle data shows BTC/CAD trading at about C$88,000 for much of Friday. It slid towards C$83,000 in the afternoon as bitcoin fell across the market.
The CAD market then broke away. The hour from 20:00 UK time on Friday reached a low of C$75,000, and the following hour touched C$61,880.
Prices kept falling overnight. Hourly lows reached C$49,611.90 shortly after midnight, C$36,700 at 06:00 and C$29,420 at 07:00 on Saturday.
The hour from 08:00 UK time printed the C$24,250 low before closing at C$45,000. By the 10:00 hour, the pair had climbed back as high as C$81,822.

Not just bitcoin
The pressure was not limited to one coin. Kraken's ticker showed a 24-hour low of 0.30001 Canadian dollars per US dollar on its
pair, against a 24-hour high of 1.43401. That pair was quoted at 1.37699 on Saturday afternoon.
CryptoSlate reported that ether and Solana hit lows of C$796 and C$32 on their CAD pairs, and that Tether's USDT briefly traded as low as C$0.0022.

Trading volumes rose sharply. About 592 BTC changed hands on BTC/CAD between 20:00 on Friday and 10:00 on Saturday, UK time, according to Kraken's hourly data. Over the previous week, the pair averaged less than 1 BTC an hour.
Why local-currency books can break
Kraken has not given a cause, and none has been confirmed. However, the episode highlights how thinner local-currency order books can drift far from global prices.

In normal conditions, arbitrage traders would buy cheap bitcoin with Canadian dollars and sell it elsewhere, pulling prices back into line. That relies on traders being able to move fresh CAD onto the exchange quickly.

Traders posting on X described opening accounts, buying bitcoin on the CAD pair and withdrawing it. Those accounts have not been independently verified. CryptoSlate noted that Kraken's status page showed no CAD spot-market incident on Saturday morning.
Regulatory backdrop
Kraken operates in Canada as a restricted dealer. Its support site says it is registered by the Ontario Securities Commission, as principal regulator, and the Canadian Securities Administrators.
The episode lands in a fragile week for crypto prices. Bitcoin fell below $60,000 on Friday, and Kraken's own
pair hit a 24-hour low of $55,100.

For clients, the decision means trades on both sides of the gap are final. Sellers who hit bids far below market prices have no reversal from Kraken, while buyers keep coins acquired at a steep discount.
